headlines.text: It was 2025 when the AEW World Tag Team Titles had a new owner by the end of the night as FTR vs. Brodido battled it out, appearing on Full Gear, rated 8.73 ? a match fans still talk about ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. It marked FTR's 20th match with the title on the line. FTR dethroned Brodido for the AEW World Tag Team Championship in a hard-hitting battle between two of the promotion's best tag teams.

It was 2023 when Jon Moxley vs. Mark Briscoe met in a Continental Classic League Match, in the show-closing main event slot on Dynamite, rated 7.60 ? a well-worked match, part of the special Thanksgiving Eve '23 card.
That Friday in 2024, Briscoe, Ishii & Romero made a statement, debuting in the main event as a team, appearing on Rampage, rated 5.84.

secondaries.text: Looking back to 2025, when gold changed shoulders as the AEW TNT Title found a new champion as Mark Briscoe vs. Kyle Fletcher battled it out in a No DQ match, appearing on Full Gear, rated 9.00 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype ? ending the champion's reign at 9 defenses. It was the 120th time the AEW TNT Title had been on the line, a genuinely rare milestone for that title. Mark Briscoe dethroned Kyle Fletcher for the TNT Championship in a brutal No Disqualification match, the stipulation itself born from Briscoe's refusal to join the Don Callis Family if he lost.

Turning the clock back to 2025: history was made as Ricochet vs. Bobby Lashley vs. Claudio Castagnoli vs. Daniel Garcia vs. Kevin Knight vs. Mark Davis vs. Matt Menard vs. Mike Bailey vs. Orange Cassidy vs. Roderick Strong vs. Shelton Benjamin vs. Wheeler Yuta contested the very first AEW National Title match in a Casino Gauntlet match, appearing on Full Gear, rated 7.33 ? a strong outing. Ricochet outlasted a stacked 12-man Casino Gauntlet field ? including Lashley, Castagnoli, Garcia, Knight, Davis, Menard, Bailey, Cassidy, Strong, Benjamin and Yuta ? to become the inaugural AEW National Champion.

On this day in 2025, El Sky Team vs. Hechicero, Okada & Takeshita etched their names into history in the first-ever CMLL World Trios Titles match, appearing on Full Gear, rated 6.74. El Sky Team's M?stico hit La M?stica on Hechicero to retain the CMLL World Trios Championship, capitalizing on a shocking mid-match betrayal when Okada turned on his own Don Callis Family partner Takeshita.
